comments.content: The pronoun "jego" is an ungrammatical literal calque of the English "its app data": the implied antecedents here ("wersja", "aplikacja") are feminine and would require "jej", and "dane aplikacji" already expresses possession, so the extra possessive is redundant and reads poorly to Polish users. Suggested copy: "Odinstalowanie %1$s usunie dane aplikacji." (The other locales in this PR — ru, tr, zh-rCN, zh-rTW — render the same source string naturally.)

comments.content: The override pair is built with `ButtonDefaults.buttonColors(...)` regardless of variant, discarding each variant's own defaults. This is invisible while overrides are only used with enabled Text buttons (the current DetailsRoot call sites), but it becomes a visual bug as soon as an overridden button is disabled or a non-Text variant is used: `buttonColors` keeps Material3's default `disabledContainerColor = onSurface @12%`, so a disabled overridden Text/Tonal/Outline button draws a grey pill where the variant (and MangaButton, which just multiplies alpha on the transparent container) stays transparent. It also silently replaces the Destructive variant's `colors.error`/`colors.onError`. Build the override with the same factory as the variant so only the enabled colors change, e.g. per-variant `ButtonDefaults.textButtonColors(containerColor = containerColor, contentColor = contentColor)`, `filledTonalButtonColors(...)`, `outlinedButtonColors(...)`, and `buttonColors(...)` for Primary/Destructive.
comments.suggestion_code:
val overrideColors =
        if (containerColor != Color.Unspecified && contentColor != Color.Unspecified) {
            when (variant) {
                KomiButtonVariant.Tonal ->
                    ButtonDefaults.filledTonalButtonColors(
                        containerColor = containerColor,
                        contentColor = contentColor,
                    )
                KomiButtonVariant.Outline ->
                    ButtonDefaults.outlinedButtonColors(
                        containerColor = containerColor,
                        contentColor = contentColor,
                    )
                KomiButtonVariant.Text ->
                    ButtonDefaults.textButtonColors(
                        containerColor = containerColor,
                        contentColor = contentColor,
                    )
                else ->
                    ButtonDefaults.buttonColors(
                        containerColor = containerColor,
                        contentColor = contentColor,
                    )
            }

comments.content: Three buttons in a non-wrapping `Row` will overflow in shipped locales at default font scale. Rough widths at Sm size in Russian (ru): "Отмена" + "Сначала удалить" + "Всё равно установить" plus paddings/gaps exceed the ~280dp content width of a typical 360dp-phone dialog. Because `Row` never wraps and each `KomiButton` uses a fixed `height(metrics.height)`, the overflowing labels are clipped or drawn outside the dialog — and the clipping gets worse with accessibility font scales (ru/hi are the longest of the 14 locales touched). Fix: use `FlowRow` so the two groups wrap onto a second line when they don't fit (keeps the cancel-left/choices-right grouping on wide surfaces), or fall back to a vertical stack on narrow widths. (`FlowRow` may need `@OptIn(ExperimentalLayoutApi::class)` depending on the foundation version.)

comments.content: The elapsed check is wall-clock based and doesn't handle clock skew. If the system clock moves backwards after the write (NTP correction, manual change — very plausible on desktop), `now - settledAt` goes negative and still satisfies `< INSTALL_SETTLE_WINDOW_MS`, so update checks stay silently suppressed for the entire skew *plus* the window (a 1-hour setback disables checks for 1h30m). Treat a negative delta as outside the window so the guard only suppresses genuine post-write checks; a forward jump then merely shortens the window, which is benign.
